title: Tenant behavioral change detector for usage/cost/latency
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a tenant-level behavioral-change detector that surfaces non-obvious shifts in usage, cost, and latency patterns (e.g., mode shifts, slow drifts, abrupt structural changes) and routes high-confidence alerts to the Console alerting pipeline with actionable context.

Problem: Current rule-based spike detectors miss subtle but high-business-impact changes (e.g., gradual increase in KV-cache misses causing cost drift, or a change in per-tenant prompt length distribution resulting in latency regressions). We need a detector that: 1) models per-tenant baselines with seasonality and feature correlations; 2) identifies structural changes vs normal variance; 3) attaches feature-level explanations and an estimated dollar/latency impact; 4) deduplicates noisy notifications and ties to routing policies (Slack channel vs PagerDuty).

Scope and non-goals: Scope covers backend pipeline components and API to emit enriched alerts into existing Console alerting (no UI work in this ticket). Non-goal: extensive front-end investigation or long-running on-call automation to remediate incidents.

Key design points: 
- Per-tenant multivariate baseline: use rolling-window feature vectors (tokens/session, avg-generation-latency, batch-size distribution, prefix-cache-hit-rate, quantized-model-variant-usage) with exponentiated-seasonal decomposition.
- Change detection: ensemble of (i) CUSUM for abrupt shifts, (ii) online Mahalanobis-distance outlier score for multivariate deviation, (iii) drift detector for gradual slope changes. Combine scores into calibrated confidence using historical false-positive calibration per tenant size tier.
- Explainability: compute top-3 contributing features and delta relative to baseline; compute estimated 24h cost delta using simple unit-cost model. Attach a short natural-language summary for the alert payload.
- Deduplication & suppression: group alerts by root-cause tags and tenant for 1h sliding window; lower-severity alerts can be batched into a daily digest.
- Routing: map high-confidence alerts to PagerDuty (SRE) and medium-confidence to Slack #console-alerts; include a one-click link to the incident runbook and the per-tenant dashboard.

Telemetry/observability goals: instrument precision/recall by synthetic injections on staging, log detector decisions, and surface an alert health dashboard (alert volume, FP rate, mean time to acknowledge).

Deliverables: 1) backend pipeline job + schema for enriched alerts; 2) calibration job to tune thresholds per-tenant tier; 3) annotated runbook and dashboard links; 4) integration tests and canary on 5 pilot tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Backend job produces enriched alert JSON to the alerts topic with fields: tenant_id, confidence, top_features, estimated_cost_delta, recommended_routing
False positive rate < 3% on synthetic injections for pilot tenants and recall >= 85% for injected regressions > 10% effect size
Alerts include a one-line natural language summary and link to per-tenant dashboard and runbook
Deduplication groups similar alerts within a 1h sliding window and prevents duplicate PagerDuty pages for the same root cause
Calibration job can be re-run weekly and stores per-tenant threshold metadata in the telemetry config table
implementation_notes: Pipeline: extend usage-telemetry ingestion job to emit per-tenant feature vectors into kafka.topic 'tenant-features' (schema v2)
Change detector service: serverless job running every 5m consuming 'tenant-features' and writing to 'enriched-alerts' topic
Calibration: offline Spark job using 90d history to derive baseline covariances and seasonality factors; store metadata in config DB
Explainability: lightweight SHAP-like scoring (feature deltas weighted by historical variance) to avoid heavyweight models
Backfill: run calibration on last 45 days and run detector in dry-run mode for 2 weeks against pilot tenants
Routing: reuse existing alert-transformer lambda to map enriched-alerts to Slack/PagerDuty with new routing table entries
